newsitem.title: USA: USDA lowers U.S. milk support price to $10.20/cwt.
newsitem.headline: USDA lowers U.S. milk support price to $10.20/cwt.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday said that the support price for milk will be $10.20 per 100 pounds in 1997, down 15 cents from the 1996 level.
The adjustment was required by the farm bill and will be effective January 1.

USDA's Commodity Credit Corp (CCC) also said its purchase price for butter will be unchanged at $0.6500 per pound in 1997, but said it will reduce its purchase price for non-fat dry milk by 1.8 cent per pound to $1.0470.
CCC said it was maintaining the butter purchase price so that the drop in the milk support price would "have the least effect on milk prices received by producers."

The purchase price for block cheddar and barrel cheese will both be reduced by 1.5 cents per pound to $1.1300 and $1.100 per pound respectively. USDA said because market prices for these products are above the new purchases prices, it "expects no negative effect on market prices."

The department said the announced price of $10.20 per 100 lb is for milk with annual average milkfat content of 3.67 percent. The support price adjusted to a milkfat content of 3.5 percent is $10.10 per 100 lb, it said.
